newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FHA cuts mortgage insurance premium.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FHA cuts mortgage insurance premium.

text.p: The Federal Housing Administration has cut its up-front mortgage insurance premium for first-time home buyers by 12.5 percent, the Department of Housing and Urban Development said on Thursday.

The reduction, the third since 1993, will save home buyers $200 in closing costs on an average mortgage of $85,000, it said. Taken together, the three reductions offer an average home buyer savings of $1,200.
The decision reduces the FHA premium for first-time home buyers to 1.75 percent of the value an FHA-insured loan from two percent.
